s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with radiation to the back, associated with nausea, vomiting, and respiratory distress
salient_findings: Worsening epigastric pain radiating to the back
Pleural effusion with positive amylase and lipase
key_facts: 43-year-old woman with a history of remote alcohol use disorder
Presented with worsening epigastric pain radiating to the back
Associated with nausea, vomiting, and early satiety
Tachycardic and tachypneic with an oxygen requirement of 4 L
Ascitic fluid positive for amylase >1000 U/L
Pleural fluid: transudative with positive amylase and lipase

shortlist.label: Acute Pancreatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with worsening epigastric pain radiating to the back, elevated lipase, and imaging studies showing acute interstitial pancreatitis

shortlist.label: Pancreatic Pseudocyst
shortlist.why_kept: CT abdomen and pelvis findings showed a 6 × 7 cm pseudocyst causing gastric outlet obstruction

shortlist.label: Pancreatic Ductal Disruption
shortlist.why_kept: ERCP findings showed leakage into peritoneal cavity and fistula extending toward diaphragm

shortlist.label: Gastric Outlet Obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with nausea, vomiting, and early satiety, and imaging studies showed gastric outlet obstruction due to pancreatic pseudocyst

shortlist.label: Pancreaticopleural Fistula
shortlist.why_kept: Pleural fluid was transudative with positive amylase and lipase, and imaging studies showed a large, right-sided pleural effusion

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with worsening epigastric pain radiating to the back, nausea, vomiting, and early satiety, along with laboratory findings of elevated lipase and amylase in ascitic and pleural fluid, is consistent with acute pancreatitis. The presence of a pseudocyst and pancreatic ductal disruption are complications that can occur in the setting of acute pancreatitis.

rejected.label: Pancreatic Pseudocyst
rejected.why: While the patient has a pseudocyst, it is a complication of the underlying condition rather than the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pancreatic Ductal Disruption
rejected.why: This is a complication that occurred in the setting of acute pancreatitis, rather than the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Gastric Outlet Obstruction
rejected.why: This is a symptom or complication of the underlying condition, rather than the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pancreaticopleural Fistula
rejected.why: While the patient has a fistula, it is a complication of the underlying condition rather than the primary diagnosis.

gold: Complete pancreatic divisum with pancreatic-pleural fistula
